## Hold made legal — the trigger is the one-package margin the card measured

devx lane PM, session `session_01PfaSTikked61BkcsB5Rn69`, round 13. Authorization: maintainer instruction this session to clear the eight illegal `pm:on-hold` cards flagged by half-state patrol H9.

Held with **no `Restart-when:` in either channel** — illegal. Repairing, because this card measured a genuine one-package margin and that margin is exactly a checkable condition.

```
Restart-when: the coverage accident stops holding — i.e. the ledgered dependency closure
  gains a member that lint.yml's preceding "Build workspace packages" step does not build.
  One-line predicate: the set difference C \ (turbo package set of
  --filter='./packages/*' --filter='./examples/*^...') is non-empty, where C is
  check-type-check-debt's own closure enumeration. Today that difference is exactly
  {@objectstack/service-knowledge}, reached only because examples/app-todo depends on it.
Restart-touch: .github/workflows/lint.yml, examples/app-todo/package.json
```

⭐ **The `Restart-touch` on `examples/app-todo/package.json` is the load-bearing half**, and it is why this card is worth keeping rather than closing. The card's own measurement: of the **55** packages in the ledgered closure, the preceding step covers all 55 — but `@objectstack/service-knowledge` is reached **only** through `./examples/*^...`, i.e. purely because `examples/app-todo` happens to depend on it. ⇒ **One manifest edit in an example app can silently break the ordering contract**, and nothing would say so. That is the specific, cheap trigger a hold needs, and it names the file.

⚠️ Restated so a future owner does not misread the risk as bigger than it is: post-#8330 the drift this would catch is already **loud in the direction that matters** — the gate refreshes with its own filters before measuring, so a narrower workflow filter ends in the `unbuiltClosure()` refusal and a wider one only costs cache hits. Neither can make CI measure a different world than a local run, which is what #8271 was. What a pin buys is protection of the **ordering claim itself**, which currently rests on a set inclusion no test asserts.

⭐ And the reason it stays cheap when it does wake: `scripts/check-type-check-coverage.mjs`'s `observed()` **already reads `.github/workflows/lint.yml`** and already derives CI-wiring facts from it that its `evaluate()` asserts. A third derived fact rides the existing `--self-test` that two jobs already invoke — no new gate, no new `lint.yml` step — and lets the filters be single-sourced in the script instead of hand-copied.

⛔ Per the card's own closing instruction, whoever picks this up must **decide against that trade deliberately, not assume it**.
